$comment: ADOPTION MANIFEST (arch step 2, S0) — CONTRACT-INTENT-FACTS-DESIGN-2026-07-26 §'The adoption rule'.
THE RULE: no field ships without, in the same change train, a named producer with a
producer-verified test, a named consumer with a consumer-verified test, or an explicit
dark-state entry carrying a removal date.
WHY: this estate already shipped three meaning fields with no producer at all. Nothing
failed, so nobody noticed across two minor versions. The rows below record that failure
as measured fact, not as a plan. Enforced by scripts/check-adoption-manifest.mjs.
WHAT COUNTS AS A PRODUCER TEST: a test that FAILS if the producer stops emitting the
field. A test asserting the field is OPTIONAL on the wire is not a producer test.
WHAT COUNTS AS A CONSUMER TEST: a test that FAILS if the consumer stops USING the value.
A test asserting the field survives parsing is a transport test, not a consumer test —
it passes just as happily when the value is parsed and then thrown away. Transport-only
evidence goes in `notes`, never in `producer_test`/`consumer_test`. Conflating the two
is how a field reaches `enforced` while still being decorative.
EVIDENCE BASIS: counted 2026-07-26 against each repo's authoritative_ref in repo-map.json
(staging for the four services, main for schemas), NOT against main. Positive control:
`assistant_text` = 543 files / 3815 lines in CEE staging, 117 files / 533 lines in UI
staging, so the counting method demonstrably finds producers when they exist.

states.declared: the field exists in the contract; no verified producer and no verified consumer
states.produced_dark: a producer emits it behind a flag/dark, with a producer test; no verified consumer
states.consumed_dark: a consumer reads it behind a flag/dark, with a consumer test; no verified producer
states.enforced: both sides verified by named tests; the field may be made required

fields.consumer_test: ui:src/v5/__tests__/responseParser.declaredKeysReachStrict.spec.ts::C1: every key OlumiResponseSchema DECLARES reaches strict validation > the sample map covers every declared key (fail-loud drift guard on the one mirror)
notes: THE POSITIVE CONTROL ROW, and deliberately NOT marked `enforced`.
Adoption is not in doubt — 543 files / 3815 lines in cee@staging, 117 / 533 in ui@staging.
But by this manifest's own definitions neither reference above is the right KIND of test:
the CEE one pins the wire SURFACE and the UI one proves the key reaches strict validation.
Both would pass if the text were emitted empty and never rendered.
Marking it `enforced` on that evidence is exactly the sloppiness S0 exists to stop, so it
stays `produced_dark` until someone writes the two tests that actually fail on regression.
It is in the manifest to prove the checker runs against real references that resolve on
disk — run with OLUMI_ESTATE_ROOT set and both paths are verified to exist.
